earlier_scan.source_named: Alviar-Calinawagan, Elizabeth. 1995. Isang grammatical iskets ng Kalinga [Pahanan Agta of San Mariano, Isabela]. University of the Philippines MA thesis, 127pp.

sources.citation: Reid, Lawrence A. 1994. Possible Non-Austronesian Lexical Elements in Philippine Negrito Languages. Oceanic Linguistics 33(1): 37-72 (author's repaginated version, ScholarSpace 10125/32986).
sources.note: Lexical paper; only remark is editorial: 'Where stress has been indicated, it is marked as an acute accent on the stressed vowel.' North Agta lists are grouped regionally (Southern Isabela etc.); no Pahanan-specific stress statement.
Bibliography only: Robinson & Lobel 2013; Ethnologue; (descriptive list adds Alviar-Calinawagan 1995).

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. (sec. 3.2.13 'Pahanan and Dinapigue Agta', pp. 88-89; fn. on diacritic conventions p. 196; sec. 8.2.9)
sources.note: Nothing on Pahanan stress. Sec. 3.2.13 states that apart from Robinson & Lobel (2012/2013) and a few lexical items in Reid (1994b) 'virtually no data for either of these languages [Pahanan, Dinapigue Agta] has appeared in the literature'. Pahanan forms cited elsewhere carry lexical accent marks (e.g. digê 'blood') under his Tagalog-style diacritic convention, but no rule is stated.

sources.citation: Robinson, Laura C. 2011. Dupaningan Agta: Grammar, vocabulary, and texts. Pacific Linguistics 635. Canberra: ANU. (ch. 2, comparative Northeastern Luzon tables 2.4-2.5)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5662 .R62 2012
sources.note: Phonology chapter is for Dupaningan only ('Stress is phonemic in Dupaningan Agta'). Pahanan Agta appears only in comparative tables from her fieldnotes, with stress marked on cited forms (ugés 'wash', bilóʔ 'widow', agdénan 'ladder', bitúʔ 'stone', bigú 'new', digúm 'needle', dilán 'road'); no statement about Pahanan stress placement.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason (requester). 2009. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2009-086 and Request for New Language Code Element 'Agta, Pahanan' [apf]. ISO 639-3 Registration Authority.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; documents the split from Paranan (r > h shift, distinct substratum) and states 'No significant body of literature and research exists on these languages'; lists as sources only Robinson 2008, Robinson & Lobel (in prep.) and Lobel (in prep.), plus SIL Bible translators M. & M. Chiong.

sources.citation: Robinson, Laura C. 2008. Dupaningan Agta: Grammar, vocabulary and texts. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Dupaningan only (sec. 2.2.2.5 'Stress is phonemic in Dupaningan Agta'); Pahanan Agta ('Palanan Dumagat') mentioned as a neighbouring, partly mutually intelligible language; nothing on its stress.

sources.citation: Alviar-Calinawagan, Elizabeth. 1995. Isang grammatical iskets ng Kalinga. MA thesis, University of the Philippines (Diliman). 127 pp. [Tagalog; 'Kalinga' = Agta of San Mariano, Isabela, classed by Glottolog under agta1234]

sources.note: Glottolog's sole descriptive reference for agta1234; a 127-page grammar sketch will normally have a ponolohiya section with a line on diin (stress).

sources.citation: Robinson, Laura C. & Jason William Lobel. 2013. The Northeastern Luzon Subgroup of Philippine Languages. Oceanic Linguistics 52(1): 125-168.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only published linguistic survey that includes Pahanan Agta first-hand data (both authors did fieldwork on it); has a phonology section for the NE Luzon languages and is the most likely place for a sentence on (contrastive) stress in Pahanan/Proto-Northeastern-Luzon.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. Kaipuleohone / fieldwork audio collections: Pahanan Agta wordlists and sentences (University of Hawai'i Digital Language Archive); Robinson, Laura C. PARADISEC collection LR1 (NE Luzon Agta recordings).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Primary recordings with stress-marked elicitation wordlists; would allow first-hand verification of stress placement if no prose statement exists.

sources.citation: Chiong, Democrito Diez & Marianne Chiong. 1990. Phonemics and morphophonemics of Palanan-Agta. Unpublished manuscript, 18 pp. SIL Philippines; SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 43464 (draft version, n.d., 17 pp.: entry 43462 'Palanan-Agta phonemics and morphophonemics').
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.note: An 18-page SIL phonemic statement (subject 'Phonological Description') will list segmental phonemes and normally has a suprasegmental paragraph stating whether stress/length is phonemic; for a Northeastern Luzon Agta language it is expected to state contrastive stress and no lexical tone, but the text was not seen.

tone.says: An 18-page SIL phonemic statement (subject 'Phonological Description') will list segmental phonemes and normally has a suprasegmental paragraph stating whether stress/length is phonemic; for a Northeastern Luzon Agta language it is expected to state contrastive stress and no lexical tone, but the text was not seen.
